sources.title: Radford M. Neal, “MCMC Using Hamiltonian Dynamics,” Handbook of Markov Chain Monte Carlo, Chapter 5
sources.locator: Complete 50-page chapter PDF inspected. Relevant ranges in the actual hosted chapter: §§5.2.1–5.2.3.3, printed pp. 114–121/PDF pp. 1–8; §§5.3.1–5.3.3.1, printed pp. 122–127/PDF pp. 9–14; §§5.4.4.1–5.4.4.2, printed pp. 139–141/PDF pp. 26–28.
sources.retrieval_history: The complete author-hosted PDF was opened and inspected. The task/design locators using §§2.x–4.x do not match this hosted edition: its relevant material is numbered §§5.2–5.4. No retrieval failure occurred.

contents.name: §5.2.1.1 Equations of Motion; §5.2.1.2 Potential and Kinetic Energy; §5.2.1.3 One-Dimensional Example
contents.reason: The source gives Hamilton equations, the quadratic kinetic energy and Gaussian momentum convention, and the harmonic oscillator. The local definition states full normalizer and regularity hypotheses.

contents.name: §5.2.2.1 Reversibility; §5.2.2.2 Conservation of the Hamiltonian; §5.2.2.3 Volume Preservation; §5.2.2.4 Symplecticness
contents.reason: The section motivates the exact-flow invariants. Its volume discussion is informal; the local theorem supplies the complete variational and change-of-variables proof with explicit completeness and Countable Choice hypotheses.

contents.name: §5.2.3.1 Euler’s Method; §5.2.3.2 A Modification of Euler’s Method; §5.2.3.3 The Leapfrog Method
contents.reason: The source gives the kick/drift update and discusses shear structure. The carrier defines the general SPD-mass composition directly, without importing the source’s diagonal-mass restriction.

contents.name: §5.2.3.3 The Leapfrog Method: reversibility and volume preservation of the shears
contents.reason: The source motivates the reversible, volume-preserving integrator. The local proof handles merely C1 potentials by section translation and uses classical Jacobians only under C2 regularity.

contents.name: §5.3.1 Probability and the Hamiltonian: Canonical Distributions; §5.3.2 The Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Algorithm; §5.3.2.1 The Two Steps of the HMC Algorithm
contents.reason: The source separates momentum refresh from the Metropolis phase update and specifies the momentum flip, Hamiltonian correction, and rejection self-transition. The local algorithm generalizes to SPD mass matrices.

contents.name: §5.3.2.2 Proof That HMC Leaves the Canonical Distribution Invariant
contents.reason: Neal’s proof uses an informal small-region partition argument. The local theorem replaces it with a complete graph-flow density argument and composes the phase kernel with refresh and projection.

contents.name: §5.3.2.3 Ergodicity of HMC
contents.reason: The source’s typical ergodicity and convergence discussion needs conditions beyond invariance. This page proves target invariance only and explicitly makes no irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence, or mixing-rate claim.

contents.name: §5.3.3.1 Trajectories for a Two-Dimensional Problem
contents.reason: The source illustrates finite-step Hamiltonian error and its effect on acceptance. The companion gives a separate one-step scalar calculation with exact coordinates and acceptance probability.

contents.name: §5.2.1.3 One-Dimensional Example and §5.3.3.1 Gaussian HMC illustrations
contents.reason: The source’s harmonic Gaussian flow checks the exact linear solution. The companion solves the Hamilton equations explicitly, checks completeness, and computes the flipped endpoint.

contents.name: §5.3.2.3 discussion of periodic and near-periodic trajectories
contents.reason: The source warns that periodic trajectories can prevent movement. The companion supplies its own exact finite-step matrix calculation and proves nonconvergence from a point-mass start.

contents.name: §5.4.4.1 Creating Distributions of Increasing Dimensionality by Replication
contents.reason: The definition preserves the source’s restriction that its scaling discussion uses replicated independent-coordinate targets; it makes no general-dimensional scaling claim.

contents.name: §5.4.4.2 Scaling of HMC and Random-Walk Metropolis
contents.reason: The source’s quantitative scaling heuristic is not needed for the HMC definition or invariance theorem. Only its replicated-target hypothesis is retained as an explicit scope warning.

sources.title: Michael Betancourt, “A Conceptual Introduction to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo,” arXiv:1701.02434v2
sources.locator: Complete 60-page author-hosted arXiv PDF inspected. Relevant complete sections: §3.2 Phase Space and Hamilton’s Equations, printed pp. 22–25/PDF pp. 21–24; §3.3 The Idealized Hamiltonian Markov Transition, printed pp. 26–27/PDF pp. 25–26; §5.1 Symplectic Integrators, printed pp. 37–38/PDF pp. 36–37; §5.2 Correcting for Symplectic Integrator Error, printed pp. 38–41/PDF pp. 37–40.
sources.retrieval_history: The complete 60-page PDF was opened and inspected. The author describes the paper as a conceptual account rather than an exhaustive rigorous treatment; it is used as an independent convention and algorithm check, while every mathematical proof is supplied locally. No retrieval failure occurred.

contents.name: §3.2 Phase Space and Hamilton’s Equations
contents.reason: This section checks the phase-space, canonical target, kinetic energy and Hamilton-equation conventions. The local definition fixes the Euclidean gradient and SPD mass assumptions.

contents.name: §3.3 The Idealized Hamiltonian Markov Transition
contents.reason: The source checks the ideal-flow invariance perspective. Completeness, differentiability, energy conservation, determinant evolution, and measure preservation are proved locally.

contents.name: §5.1 Symplectic Integrators
contents.reason: The section independently checks the leapfrog splitting convention. The local map is defined as explicit kick and drift shears for general SPD mass.

contents.name: §5.1 Symplectic Integrators
contents.reason: The source motivates reversibility and preservation for symplectic integrators. The local proof gives a measure-level shear argument valid for C1 potentials.

contents.name: §5.2 Correcting for Symplectic Integrator Error
contents.reason: The section checks that the Metropolis correction accounts for finite integration error. The local algorithm retains rejected states and states the exact energy-ratio convention.

contents.name: §5.2 Correcting for Symplectic Integrator Error
contents.reason: The source confirms the correction principle. Its conceptual exposition is not used as proof; the local theorem proves the accepted-flow density and invariant position transition.

contents.name: §5.2 Correcting for Symplectic Integrator Error
contents.reason: The source distinguishes numerical energy error from corrected target invariance. The companion computes one exact scalar leapfrog step and its acceptance probability.

sources.title: OpenStax, Calculus Volume 2, §3.7 Improper Integrals, Example 3.55
sources.locator: Full relevant section inspected: §3.7, definition (3.16) of an improper integral and Example 3.55, particularly the evaluation of ∫_1^∞ e^{-x} dx as a convergent limit.
sources.retrieval_history: The complete section webpage was opened; the improper-integral definition, comparison theorem, and Example 3.55 computation were inspected. Its positive-tail calculation supports one side of the local lemma; the local proof supplies the two-sided Lebesgue-measure argument.

contents.name: §3.7 Definition (3.16) and Example 3.55: convergence of the exponential tail integral
contents.reason: The source evaluates the positive exponential tail by truncating at t and taking the finite limit. The authored lemma uses this as a check; its own complete proof gives a geometric interval bound and handles both tails under the stated Countable Choice assumption.
